page: OVHcloud h100-1520 is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance within the Cloud GPU family, hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The compute configuration consists of 120 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs operating at a 3.0 GHz clock speed, backed by 1520 GB of system memory, delivering approximately 12.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. Accelerated compute is provided by four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs delivering a total of 320 GB of VRAM.

For high-speed I/O and data staging, the instance includes 15,560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage bundled directly into the hardware configuration. System networking operates at a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the standard provisioning, requiring network allocation planning for public egress or ingress.

The substantial ratio of memory to compute combined with multi-GPU acceleration positions the h100-1520 for demanding artificial intelligence and high-performance computing tasks. Key target workloads include distributed deep learning training, large language model fine-tuning and inference, and high-throughput data processing. Delivering high density across GPU, RAM, and local NVMe capacity within a single server limits inter-node communication overhead for complex parallel jobs.
description: OVHcloud h100-1520 is a high-density accelerator instance in the Cloud GPU family, built on the KVM hypervisor. The instance combines 120 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running at 3.0 GHz with 1520 GB of system RAM, equating to roughly 12.67 GB per core. Acceleration is provided by four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs offering a cumulative 320 GB of VRAM. For high-speed data handling and intermediate checkpointing, the system incorporates 15,560 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network connection. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Combining extensive GPU VRAM, substantial system memory, and expansive local flash storage within a single system, the h100-1520 is suited for large language model pre-training, complex deep learning fine-tuning, large-scale matrix computations, and demanding parallel data analysis workloads where multi-GPU synchronization and high I/O throughput are paramount.
